title: The relative efficiency of sequential tests
summary: While many statistical procedures rely on a fixed sample size, sequential methods allow a decision-maker to adapt the sample size to achieve a given precision. In this way, sequential tests reduce the average number of observations required to achieve a given power of the test -- but by how much? To address this question, we focus on the scenario of testing the unknown drift of a Brownian motion, comparing the Wald sequential probability ratio test with tests that use a pre-determined fixed sample size.
